note: Families split by machine: f2 plus the heavy f0 jobs 3 and 4 on machine 0, f1 then the light f0 jobs on machine 1, with one maintenance on each machine before the low-weight tail. Risk: machine 1 runs long and the f0 tail ends very late.
Same split as plan 1 but with no maintenance. Risk: wear piles up and makes the low-weight tail later.
Machine 0 runs only f2 with no setups; machine 1 runs f1 with the f0 block placed early for jobs 3 and 4. Risk: two extra setups on machine 1 push heavy jobs 0 and 14 late.
High-weight jobs go first on both machines and low-weight jobs go after maintenance. Risk: the f2/f0 switches on machine 0 add setups and make job 9 late.
Pure EDD order, alternating jobs between machines and ignoring families. Risk: almost every job needs a setup, which loses a lot of time.
Frequent maintenance, about every 3-4 jobs, to keep wear low. Risk: each 9-unit maintenance and the late f0 jobs 3 and 4 cost more than the wear saved.
Machine 1 gets only f1; machine 0 gets f2 and all of f0. Risk: the load is badly unbalanced and the f2 jobs on machine 0 run very late.
Load is balanced by moving the f2 tail (10, 18) to machine 1 after maintenance; machine 0 mixes f2 and f0. Risk: the family switches on machine 0 cost about 12 time units in setups.
